findings.title: Materials' 66-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.28x forward but 35.88x trailing, a 66-point percentile gap between the two lenses. The market is underwriting 120 percent earnings growth, which would be the steepest margin recovery in the sector's recent history.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' forward multiple collapses despite rich history
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward P/E sits at the 45th percentile while its trailing multiple remains at the 93rd, a 48-point disconnect. The 35 percent compression implies analysts expect a 53 percent earnings surge, a bet that staples can suddenly grow like cyclicals.

findings.title: Energy's forward multiple jumps while trailing stays rich
findings.body: Energy's forward percentile rose 18 points in a month to 51, yet its trailing P/E still sits at the 83rd percentile. The 32-point gap between lenses means the market is pricing in 58 percent earnings growth, but the sector's own history suggests such optimism has been fleeting.
